scope: Selected Bond branches described in Grubbs (1958), checked against selected original page images. These are related firms, not independent matched controls.
money: Nominal dollars. Accounting categories differ; no return-on-capital ranking is calculated.

observations.claim: Cabra predecessor established in 1899; relocation to Cuervo around 1902-1903, exact date unresolved
Reported company net profits positive in all twelve years 1904-1915
Merchandise, credit, sheep, wool and shipping combined; sheep investment exceeds merchandise inventory in 1913-1915
Grubbs describes the operating Cuervo firm in 1958

branches.limit: Secondary reconstruction from company sources. Positive accounting profit does not establish a return exceeding the owners' alternative opportunities. No final closure date.

observations.claim: Bond acquired an existing mercantile and sheep business in 1892
Merchandise and sheep net profits change relative importance
Inventory and receivable valuation practices varied

branches.limit: The two profit lines are not assumed to equal total company earnings. Valuation changes and withdrawals complicate comparisons. Roy is not counted as a confirmed retail branch.

branches.firm: G. W. Bond & Bro. Mercantile Co.

observations.claim: 1913 net profit of 174.41 differs from Table 52 earnings of about 1700 because that table includes 1500 interest on capital stock
Sheep handled at Encino before 1908 were booked at Espanola
The 1909 sheep investment account shows zero, but 1434 sheep were on hand and omitted from that inventory
Sheep on rent: 12861 in 1914 and 14392 in 1915

branches.limit: The location of an account is not necessarily the location of production. Registered-office moves and an undated insolvency caption are not verified store-closing dates.

branches.place: Rosa, Rio Arriba County (NOT Santa Rosa)

observations.claim: Organized March 13, 1912; 16000 capital, four equal partners
1915 sheep investment of 6767.65 represented 2935 ewes, all leased
Manager A. H. Long threatened to withdraw sheep from Porfirio Gallegos for shopping elsewhere; Bond advised against retaliation
observations.original_targets: Letter Book 58, June 24 and June 29, 1915, pp. 590 and 652; current finding-aid volume 83; originals not inspected

observations.claim: Cash strain required a Bond-backed loan despite reported profits
Grubbs reports firm moved to Albuquerque in 1920 and dissolved in 1923

branches.limit: Corporate events do not date the disappearance of all Rosa services. Credit sales are not cash collections, and company earnings may include sheep returns.

independent_check.case: Burguete v. G. W. Bond & Bro. Mercantile Co., 43 N.M. 97, 85 P.2d 749, 1938-NMSC-075, December 20, 1938
independent_check.evidence: Court opinion describes merchandise, ranching, partido sheep, land security, rancher debts and a 90000 refinancing loan. It reports an agreement routing the plaintiffs' business through the corporation while that loan remained unpaid.
independent_check.result: Affirmed rejection of the claimed debt-cancellation agreement: the manager lacked authority for it and the corporation did not ratify it.
independent_check.limit: Firm and manager match the Encino company history, but the opinion does not locate every transaction at Encino. Selected litigation involving two ranchers, not a typical Cuervo contract or an estimate of prevalence. Web-extracted opinion, not a certified original scan.
